core_obligations: Choose a hypercovering (proof lines 2232-2248): take an etale hypercovering of the base with affine components in every degree, using the hypercovering lemma together with the operation of taking disjoint unions in each degree; base changing along the morphism gives an etale hypercovering of the source with induced structure morphisms.

Build the local data (proof lines 2248-2270): on each affine component there is a relative dualizing complex over the corresponding affine piece, and the structure morphisms of the hypercoverings induce unique comparison isomorphisms between the pullbacks of these pairs; assembling the pieces over each degree and using uniqueness, one obtains comparison isomorphisms between degrees which satisfy the transitivity condition needed for a cartesian system.

Glue (proof lines 2270-2314): the hypotheses of the gluing lemma for cartesian derived modules are satisfied, so there is a quasi-coherent complex on the source together with an isomorphism to the degree zero piece compatible with the two face maps; the vanishing of negative self extensions, valid locally and preserved by pullback, allows a second gluing lemma to produce the trace map whose restriction to the first degree agrees with the local one; by the detection lemma the resulting pair is a relative dualizing complex.
proof_roadmap: Choose an etale hypercovering with affine components.
Construct the local relative dualizing complexes and the comparison isomorphisms on the pieces.
Glue the complex and the trace map and apply the detection lemma.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the existence of a relative dualizing complex for a proper flat morphism of algebraic spaces of finite presentation (statement lines 2228-2231). The proof (proof lines 2232-2314) chooses an etale hypercovering with affine components, assembles the local relative dualizing complexes with their unique comparison isomorphisms, glues the complex and the trace map using the vanishing of negative self extensions, and applies the detection lemma. H3: a long gluing construction written out in full.
